subject: feat(catalog): support write.metadata.delete-after-commit.enabled (#3582)
body:
* feat(catalog): support write.metadata.delete-after-commit.enabled

Add the `write.metadata.delete-after-commit.enabled` table property
(default false). When it is set, catalogs that write metadata files
themselves delete the previous metadata files that fall out of the
metadata log (bounded by `write.metadata.previous-versions-max`) after
a successful commit, matching Java's
`CatalogUtil.deleteRemovedMetadataFiles`.

The shared `delete_removed_metadata_files` helper diffs the base and
committed metadata logs and deletes best-effort, logging failures
without failing the commit. It is wired into the memory, SQL and Glue
catalogs. REST and S3 Tables are left out because the server or
service owns metadata file cleanup, and HMS does not support commits
yet.

Address review: test that cleanup reads the property from the new

subject: fix(expr): prune In predicates that straddle metrics bounds (#3144)
body:
* fix(expr): prune In predicates that straddle metrics bounds

InclusiveMetricsEvaluator and ManifestEvaluator tested each bound against
the full literal set, so IN lists with values both below lower and above
upper were not pruned. Narrow the set the way Java, PyIceberg, and
StrictMetricsEvaluator::not_in already do.

* fix(expr): check In literals against both bounds together

Apply review feedback: use any() instead of clone/retain, and prune
straddling In predicates in RowGroupMetricsEvaluator too.

* refactor(expr): share In bound check across metrics evaluators

The three In evaluators used the same match. Pull it into a crate-private helper.

* fix(expr): treat NaN metrics bounds as unbounded for In pruning

A valid min or max still prunes when the other bound is NaN, instead of
bailing on both sides.

* chore(deps): bump ctutils and tokio past rustsec advisories

The security audit fails on ctutils 0.4.2 and warns on tokio 1.53.1. Both versions are already on main. 0.4.5 and 1.53.3 clear the two advisories.

* fix(expr): keep incomparable In literals from pruning

ge and le are false when Datum::partial_cmp is None, so any_literal_in_bounds treated those literals as outside the range. Prune only when every literal is provably below the lower bound or above the upper bound.

* fix(expr): look up row group stats once for In

min_value and max_value each resolved the same statistics. The In path now uses one stats_and_type_for_field_id lookup and still drops a NaN bound before the prune.

subject: fix(arrow): release a positional delete file whose load fails (#3435)
body:
* fix(arrow): release a positional delete file whose load fails

try_start_pos_del_load marks a positional delete file Loading, and only
the success path marked it Loaded. If opening or parsing the file
failed, or the load was dropped because another delete file failed,
the entry stayed Loading: a retry on the same loader, a clone of the
same ArrowReader, or a concurrent load of the same file waited for a
notification that never came.

The Load action now carries a PosDelLoadGuard. finish() marks the file
loaded; dropping the guard without finishing removes the Loading marker
and wakes the waiters. A woken waiter checks the state again and loads
the file itself if it isn't loaded, instead of assuming it is.

Closes #3434.

* refactor(arrow): assert the Loading invariant when abandoning a load

Only try_start_pos_del_load inserts into positional_deletes, and only the
guard that it returns changes the entry afterwards, so the entry is always
the guard's Loading marker when it is abandoned.

* test(arrow): cover waiters that load after an abandoned positional load

Hold the Load guard, poll load_file_for_task for the same file until it
waits, then drop the guard: the waiter loads the file itself, or returns
the open error when the file is gone. Also load a positional delete file
that opens but fails to parse, then rewrite it and load it again on the
same loader, which hangs without the guard.

* fix(arrow): return a failed positional delete load's error to its waiters

Waiters on a failed load used to retry it one after another, so a missing
file shared by many tasks was opened once per task. The load now records
its error and the tasks waiting on that attempt return it. A load dropped
without an error, when a sibling's error stops load_deletes, still lets
its waiters retry, and later calls start a new attempt either way.

Abandoning a load also tolerates a poisoned lock, since it runs from Drop.

* test(arrow): keep the sibling's load in flight when another delete file fails

On the current-thread test runtime the local filesystem never yields, so the
valid file was only loaded on the second call and its guard was never dropped
mid-load. A test storage now yields before reads and holds one file until the
test opens a gate.

* fix(arrow): pass the whole load error to waiters

subject: feat(reader)!: resolve unknown delete-file sizes lazily (#3433)
body:
* feat(reader): resolve unknown delete-file sizes lazily

Execution engines that build scan tasks themselves do not always carry a
delete file's size. Tasks planned from manifest entries keep the
recorded size; externally constructed tasks may now leave
FileScanTaskDeleteFile's file size unset, and the Parquet delete-file
loader resolves it with one metadata request when the file is first
loaded. The caching loader loads each delete file once per reader, so
the request is made once per delete file even when several data files
reference it.

FileScanTaskDeleteFile::file_size_in_bytes now returns Option<u64>.
None means unknown, so a size of 0 is no longer a sentinel and is
rejected like any other size below the Parquet footer minimum.

A failed metadata request is reported with the delete-file path while
keeping the storage error's kind and retryability. A size below the
Parquet footer minimum, whether resolved or supplied by the task, fails
the read rather than dropping the file's deletes. Deletion vectors do
not use this size and are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: unikdahal <unikdahal03@gmail.com>

* fix(reader): rely on Parquet's footer check for delete-file sizes

Parquet already rejects a size below its footer, so drop the separate
8-byte check and assert Parquet's error in the test instead.

Also document leaving the size unset when the recorded one can't be
trusted (apache/iceberg#12554), add a serde round trip for a delete file
without a size, and tidy the metadata-counting test storage.

* test(reader): drop delete-size tests covered elsewhere

Keep only the footer cases in the delete_file_loader test; the missing
file and lazy read are covered by test_load_deletes_reports_unknown_size_failures
and test_read_encrypted_positional_delete_file. Remove the equality-delete
parse test, which test_unknown_size_equality_deletes_are_resolved_once_and_cached
already covers through load_deletes.

* test(reader): resolve unknown delete sizes once under concurrent loads

* test(reader): yield in the counting storage so concurrent loads overlap

* fix(scan): keep the delete file size required in the builder

* test(reader): drop qualifications the merge made unnecessary

subject: feat(storage-opendal): configurable retry policy via opendal.retry.* and s3.retry.* (#3605)
body:
* feat(storage-opendal): read the s3.retry.* properties

The S3 operator was always wrapped in `RetryLayer::new()`: 3 retries, a 1 s
first delay, no jitter. A throttled bucket (S3 `SlowDown`) answers a burst of
requests faster than that policy gives up, and the error reaches the caller
after about 7 s.

Define Iceberg Java's `s3.retry.num-retries`, `s3.retry.min-wait-ms` and
`s3.retry.max-wait-ms` in `iceberg::io` so every S3 backend can read the same
keys, and apply them to the opendal S3 operator. Setting any of them also turns
on jitter; with none set the layer stays `RetryLayer::new()`.

Generated-by: Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5)

* feat(storage-opendal): add backend-independent opendal.retry.* properties

`opendal.retry.num-retries`, `opendal.retry.min-wait-ms` and `opendal.retry.max-wait-ms`
configure the `RetryLayer` of every backend, in the place where the `TimeoutLayer` is
applied. For S3 each `s3.retry.*` key overrides the matching `opendal.retry.*` key,
resolved per key; unset keeps OpenDAL's default. Any set key turns jitter on.

Generated-by: Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5)

* refactor(storage-opendal): keep the reviewed retry tests, add only the new cases

Restore the four tests of a767ae1e0 as they were (their S3-only semantics still hold) and
add only the generic-keys and per-key precedence cases; `s3_retry_layer` stays as a thin
wrapper of `retry_layer(true)`.

Generated-by: Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5)

* refactor(storage-opendal): resolve s3.retry.* overrides when building the S3 storage

Parse the s3.retry.* properties next to the other s3.* properties and
overlay them, per key, onto the opendal.retry.* settings of the S3
variant's client config. OpenDalClientConfig no longer knows about S3, so
retry_layer takes no backend flag and other backends neither parse nor
serialize s3.retry.*.

subject: fix(arrow): spawn data file opens on the IO runtime (#3277)
body:
* fix(arrow): spawn data file opens on the IO runtime

Opens run ahead of the reads. Once try_flatten_unordered holds
concurrency_limit_data_files streams it stops polling the opens, and a
half-read response keeps part of the HTTP/2 connection window, which
stalls every other read on that connection.

Spawning the open is what load_deletes already does.

Signed-off-by: Swanand Mulay <73115739+swanandx@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(arrow): abort the data file opens when the scan is dropped

A dropped JoinHandle detaches the task, so a cancelled scan left its opens
fetching a result nobody reads. Add a pub(crate) abort-on-drop handle and
use it for the opens.

JoinHandle already maps JoinError, so the open needs no second wrapper.

Signed-off-by: Swanand Mulay <73115739+swanandx@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(arrow): spawn only the data file open

Only the open needs to escape the polling gap, so the spawn moves inside
process() and the read() call site returns to what main has.

Two tests in pipeline.rs replace the flow control harness: an open must
proceed when nothing polls the scan, and a dropped scan must stop opening
files.

Signed-off-by: Swanand Mulay <73115739+swanandx@users.noreply.github.com>

counted_scan now builds its file with write_plain_parquet, and the tests
watch metrics().bytes_read() instead of their own request counter, so the
counting storage only adds the yield.

The comment above the spawn drops the HTTP/2 detail that #3276 already
carries.

subject: fix(encryption): reject encryption.key-id on pre-v3 tables (#3659)
body:
* fix(encryption): reject encryption.key-id on pre-v3 tables

EncryptionManager::from_table_metadata returned Ok(None) for v1/v2 tables
before reading encryption.key-id, so commits to such tables silently wrote
plaintext manifest lists and manifests. Return DataInvalid instead, matching
iceberg-python.

* fix(encryption): reject pre-v3 encryption properties on metadata updates

Reject encryption.key-id and encryption.data-key-length when creating a
table or setting properties below v3, before anything is persisted.
Pre-v3 tables that already carry them still load, so they can be
repaired by removing the properties or upgrading to v3, and snapshot

subject: feat(scan): optionally retain column statistics on FileScanTask (#3424)
body:
* feat(scan): optionally retain column statistics on FileScanTask

Add TableScanBuilder::with_column_stats, mirroring Java's
Scan.includeColumnStats. The named columns resolve to field ids at build
time with the scan's case sensitivity, and each planned FileScanTask
carries a FileScanTaskColumnStats holding the data file's value, null and
NaN counts and lower and upper bounds for only those field ids.

Retention is opt-in: by default column_stats is None, nothing is copied
from the manifest entry, and the field is omitted when a task is
serialized, so serialized tasks are unchanged.

* fix(scan): serialize column bounds as spec binary values

Bounds went through Datum's JSON encoding, which writes non-finite floats
as null and rejects many finite float values when reading them back, so a
task with such a bound serialized but failed to deserialize. Serialize
each bound as its type and the spec's single-value binary encoding, as the
DataFile JSON serde already does, so every bound round-trips exactly.

* refactor(scan): address review of column statistics retention

Retain column_sizes for the requested ids too, matching Java's
BaseFile(copy, requestedColumnIds). Share the column-name lookup and its
error with column selection, keep the requested names as an Option like
column_names so an empty list yields empty statistics, and pass the ids as
Arc<[i32]>. Skip work for an empty map when filtering, trim the struct
docs, and cover nested field names.

* fix(scan): reject column names that cannot have statistics

Struct, list and map fields have no statistics of their own, and metadata
columns are not stored in data files, so requesting stats for them
silently returned empty maps or failed with a misleading "not found"
error. Fail build() with an error that says why. Also cover bounds that
keep the manifest's type after a type promotion.

* fix(scan): promote column stats bounds to the scan schema type

A manifest written before a type promotion keeps the narrower type, so one
scan could return an int bound for one file and a long bound for another,
and Datum cannot order values of different types. Promote bounds to the
column's type in the scan schema (int to long, float to double, decimal to
a wider precision) and omit a bound that cannot be promoted.

Box the retained statistics so tasks of scans that never request them do
not grow, and add a doctest for with_column_stats.

* refactor(scan): resolve column stats types once and trim tests and docs

Resolve each requested column's type when the scan is built, so planning
no longer looks the column up in the schema for every bound of every
manifest entry. Rebuild the column stats tests on the builder, one
behavior per test, and cover list names. Drop private field docs that
repeated the getter docs, and state the decimal and date-to-timestamp
promotion rules in the struct docs.

* docs(scan): drop the date to timestamp claim from the column stats docs

A date bound under a timestamp column is stored in 4 bytes, which
Datum::try_from_bytes cannot decode as a timestamp, so the manifest read
fails before planning sees the bound. The docs described a case that
planning never handles.

body:
* fix(arrow): map Iceberg Binary to Arrow Binary instead of LargeBinary

`type_to_arrow_type` mapped `PrimitiveType::Binary` to `DataType::LargeBinary`,
which is inconsistent with both the Java implementation
(`ArrowSchemaUtil` maps Iceberg Binary to Arrow `Binary`) and parquet-rs,
which reads an unannotated Parquet `BYTE_ARRAY` column as `DataType::Binary`
by default. The mismatch forces an unnecessary cast when reading Binary
columns and diverges from the rest of the ecosystem.

Map `PrimitiveType::Binary` to `DataType::Binary`. The reverse conversion
(`arrow_schema_to_schema`), the arrow-to-literal path, and the bucket
transform already accept both `Binary` and `LargeBinary`, so externally
produced `LargeBinary` columns keep working.

Closes #2698

* fix(writer): accept LargeBinary equality columns after the Binary mapping change

With Iceberg Binary now mapped to Arrow Binary, the equality delete
projector builds its output batch against a Binary schema while reusing
the input arrays as-is, so batches carrying LargeBinaryArray equality
columns (accepted before) failed RecordBatch::try_new. Cast LargeBinary
to Binary in RecordBatchProjector::project_batch and add a regression
test. Also drop redundant `.as_slice()` in test fixtures.

* fix(arrow): accept LargeBinary source columns in partition value calculation

PartitionValueCalculator builds its result struct against the partition

identity transform passes the projected LargeBinary column through, so
StructArray::try_new failed. Move the LargeBinary -> Binary cast from
RecordBatchProjector::project_batch into project_column so both callers
get columns matching the projected schema. This also lets truncate
partitions on binary fields accept LargeBinary input.

* fix(reader): keep pages whose index bounds cannot be compared with the predicate

Page-index bounds are built with the table field type but the file's
physical literal. When the two differ, e.g. a long field read against
INT32 pages written before an int -> long promotion, a double field
against FLOAT pages, or a UINT_32 column mapped to long, the bounds
never compare with the predicate literal. Inequality and IN predicates
treated that as "cannot match" and skipped pages holding matching rows.

inequality check now treats an incomparable bound as a possible match,
and IN uses all(lt) / all(gt) instead of !any(ge) / !any(le).

* test(reader): cover a mixed UINT_32 page in the page-index evaluator

A page holding both 100 and 3_000_000_000 has a raw signed max below its
min, which pins the unsigned column order that a later bound widening has
to zero-extend rather than sign-extend.

* test(reader): cover all four inequality operators on promoted float and timestamp pages

and removed ParquetMetaData::column_index, so the tests added here no longer

subject: fix(transform): avoid overflow panic in truncate at integer minimum (#3573)
body:
* fix(transform): match Java truncate wrapping arithmetic

## Which issue does this PR close?

- Closes issue 3141.

## What changes are included in this PR?

`truncate_i32` used `rem_euclid`, while `truncate_i64` and `truncate_decimal_i128` used `(v % w + w) % w`. Both shapes differ from Iceberg Java's `TruncateUtil`, which relies on `int`/`long` overflow wrapping:

- For `truncate_i32`, `rem_euclid` never overflows, so any width above `2^30` produced a different partition value than Java.
- For the other two, the final subtraction overflowed at the integer minimum, panicking in debug builds and wrapping to the Java value only in release builds.

All three helpers now use `wrapping_sub` and `wrapping_add`, so every width reproduces the Java result in both debug and release builds. Each helper has a comment noting that the formula intentionally matches Java, so it is not "simplified" back to `rem_euclid` later. The function signatures, the public API, and the call sites are unchanged.

## Are these changes tested?

Three unit tests in `crates/iceberg/src/transform/truncate.rs`. All expected values were computed with Iceberg Java's `TruncateUtil` (1.11.0, JDK 17):

- `test_truncate_int_matches_java` covers the three `i32` cases from the issue, plus the smallest width where `(v % w) + w` can overflow (`2^30 + 1`) and a tiny value at the maximum width. Each case is checked through both `transform` on an array and `transform_literal`.
- `test_truncate_long_min_matches_java` covers `i64::MIN` with widths 1000 and `i32::MAX`, through the same two paths.
- `test_truncate_decimal_i128_min_does_not_panic` pins that the decimal path does not panic at `i128::MIN`. That value is outside the range of a 38-digit Iceberg decimal, and Java's `truncateDecimal` works on `BigInteger`, so there is no wrapping result to compare against.

Reverting the helpers to their previous bodies makes all three tests fail. For the `i64` cases the old formula happens to give the Java values once wrapped, so it is caught by the debug-build overflow panic.

## AI Disclosure

Human-led contribution. Codex and Grok Bot, working for dragonknightk, assisted with this change. All submitted content was reviewed by a human before submission.

* test(transform): document truncate wrap results and assert the i128 value

subject: feat(transaction): update the name mapping when UpdateSchemaAction adds columns (#3665)
body:
* feat(transaction): update the name mapping when UpdateSchemaAction adds columns

When a table has schema.name-mapping.default, UpdateSchemaAction now adds
entries for added columns to it in the same commit, as Java's
MappingUtil.update does: new entries go under the parent's entry, an
existing entry in the same struct loses a name an added column takes, and
deleted columns keep their entries. A mapping that fails to parse is
logged and left unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>

* fix(transaction): skip name mapping entries for additions under deleted ancestors

An addition whose parent is deleted in the same update is dropped from the
new schema, and its ID can be assigned again later. Giving it a name
mapping entry would let id-less files resolve that name to an unrelated
column. Also look up added names through a map instead of scanning the
additions for every alias.

Co-authored-by: Isaac <no-reply@databricks.com>
